As President Trump stumps for Republican candidates less than two weeks
before midterm election day, he continues to boast about his growing power
in his second term in office.
And Piers Franco Ordonez reports on now he's making his case to voters.
Trump continues to crash through barriers that he wouldn't dare

And that's the way he's really run his second term is what I call a unilateralist.
He doesn't have an ideology.

Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
With US envoy Steve Woodkopf expected to meet with Russian leader Vladimir Putin
today, President Trump is again expressing frustration with Ukraine.
We've given a lot to Ukraine.
We've got absolutely nothing back except grief, death, tremendous monetary
loss. Trump spoke to reporters in the Oval Office Tuesday after relations
with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky soured again.
Meanwhile, Zelensky says Ukraine is again receiving early warnings about
Russian attacks, but that the US is still delaying the delivery of American
Patriot missiles.
And he says Trump's decision to purchase Russian diesel fuel only empowers
Moscow. The Federal Aviation Administration has cleared the way for
airlines to put Boeing 737 MAX 10 into service.
The MAX 10 is the largest version of the Boeing's best selling airplane.
The FAA said Tuesday it has certified it for passenger service.
Certification came after years of delays due to technical and safety related
concerns. A new survey shows homebuilders are the most pessimistic they've been
about the housing market in more than 14 years.
NPR Stephen Pissaha reports a high cost of borrowing and for materials are big
reasons why builders are in a sour mood.
The National Association of Home Builders Survey for October found there has not
been this much pessimism since 2012 when the housing market was still recovering
from the Great Recession. The Association also reports that the price of goods
used for home building, including energy, was up almost 10 percent in
September year over year.
All this gloom is also showing up in new home permits in September.
They were down about 3 percent from a year ago.
There's just not much demand for buying homes right now with high mortgage
rates. The National Association of Realtors reports that pending home sales
in September were down more than 11 percent from a year earlier.
Stephen Pissaha, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
A New Jersey based food importer is challenging the Trump administration's
latest tariffs on imports from Canada.
The Geller Group took its case today, Tuesday rather, to the U.S.
Court of International Trade, arguing that the duties represent another attempt
to claim presidential tariff power that has been rejected in court.
Geller is a third generation family business that imports Canadian cheese.
A new study finds that people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
had a higher risk of dying from any cause.
But NPR's Maria Godoy reports that taking ADHD medication
is linked to a lower risk of death.
Researchers analyzed the findings of 19 studies that included data from nearly
16 million people with and without ADHD on three continents.
Some studies followed participants for more than 20 years.
They found that ADHD was linked to significantly higher risks of suicide
and injury deaths, as well as a moderately higher risk of dying from natural causes.
But they also found some evidence that this risk of mortality is lower
among people who take ADHD medication.
The researchers say the findings underscore the need for everyone
who may have ADHD to have access to accurate diagnoses and treatment.
The findings appear in the journal JAMA Network Open,
Maria Godoy and PR News.
Stocks in South Korea leading the way in Wednesday trading.
South Korea's benchmark up three percent.
Following a rally on Wall Street, Japan's Nikkei up one percent.
I'm Jael Snyder in PR News.
